data.name: Tour.WORKCENTER.Step1.Text
data.value: Inbox holds work and approval requests sent to you, My Work the work you own, and Pool the work your team can pick up.

data.name: Tour.WORKCENTER.Step2.Text
data.value: Type part of a title to narrow the list; the filter chips narrow it further by type and status.

data.name: Tour.WORKCENTER.Step3.Text
data.value: Click a row to open the work: its details, checklist, comments and history are there.

data.name: Tour.WORKCENTER.Step4.Text
data.value: Accept, Start and Complete sit on the row. Open an approval request to Approve or Reject it; to hand work to someone else, use Delegate in the opened work.

data.name: Tour.WORKCENTER.Step5.Text
data.value: Create a new task, note or meeting from here.

data.name: Tour.MYTIMESHEET.Step1.Text
data.value: Move between weeks with the arrows; Today brings you back to the current week.

data.name: Tour.MYTIMESHEET.Step2.Text
data.value: Use + Task row or + Category row to add what you worked on this week.

data.name: Tour.MYTIMESHEET.Step3.Text
data.value: Type the hours into each day's cell; the totals update as you go.

data.name: Tour.MYTIMESHEET.Step4.Text
data.value: When the week is complete, choose Submit for approval; your approver then sees it in Timesheet approvals.

data.name: Tour.TIMEAPPROVALS.Step1.Text
data.value: Weeks your team submitted for approval are listed here.

data.name: Tour.TIMEAPPROVALS.Step2.Text
data.value: Open a row to read the week, then choose Approve, or Return with a reason so it can be corrected.

data.name: Help.USERS.Purpose
data.value: Manage everyone who can sign in to your tenant: invite users, edit their details and decide whether each account is active.

data.name: Help.USERS.Step1
data.value: Narrow the list with the search box, or click “Filter”, choose “Status”, “Roles” or “Account Type” and click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.USERS.Step2
data.value: Click “Add User”, fill in “Email”, “First Name” and “Last Name” in the side panel, then click “Save” or press Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on a Mac). An invitation e-mail is sent, so a bare Enter does not save.

data.name: Help.USERS.Step3
data.value: Ask the new user to set a password through the e-mailed link; until then the status shows “Invited” and the row offers “Resend Invitation”.

data.name: Help.USERS.Step4
data.value: Open a row's actions to “View” or “Edit” a user, “Disable” or “Enable” the account, send a “Reset Password” link, or “Delete” it.

data.name: Help.USERS.Step5
data.value: To give a user roles, open the User Roles page; the “Roles” column here only shows what is already assigned.

data.name: Help.USERS.Related.ROLES
data.value: To see what each role allows

data.name: Help.ROLES.Purpose
data.value: This page lists your tenant's roles: System roles that come with the platform and Custom roles you create.

data.name: Help.ROLES.Step1
data.value: Search the list, or click “Filter”, pick “System (built-in, locked)” or “Custom (editable)” under “Type” and click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.ROLES.Step2
data.value: Click “Add Role”, enter “Name” and “Display Name” (and a “Description” if needed), then click “Save”; the name cannot be changed later.

data.name: Help.ROLES.Step3
data.value: Click the key icon “Manage Permissions” on a row to open Role Permissions with that role already selected.

data.name: Help.ROLES.Step4
data.value: Use “View”, “Edit” or “Delete” on a custom role; a system role shows a lock icon and can only be viewed.

data.name: Help.ROLES.Related.ROLEPERMISSIONS
data.value: To set what a role may do

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Purpose
data.value: This page sets what a role is allowed to do: you grant or remove permissions, grouped by module, for one role at a time.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Step1
data.value: Pick a role in the “Role” box; coming from “Manage Permissions” on the Roles page opens it with the role already selected.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Step2
data.value: Narrow the permissions with “Module”, the “Search permissions…” box, or the “All”, “Assigned” and “Unassigned” tabs.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Step3
data.value: Click an unassigned permission chip to grant it to the role; the change is saved at once.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Step4
data.value: Click an assigned chip and confirm to remove it; chips with a lock come from the baseline or a module and cannot be changed here.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Step5
data.value: Check “Selected Role” on the right for “Permission coverage” and the assigned, locked and unassigned counts.

data.name: Help.ROLEPERMISSIONS.Immediate
data.value: Granting and removing a permission; it affects every user who holds the role

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Purpose
data.value: This page links users to roles: pick one user, then give them roles or take roles away.

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Step1
data.value: Pick a person in the “User” box to see the roles they hold and the ones they do not.

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Step2
data.value: Narrow the roles with the “Search Roles” box or the “All”, “Assigned” and “Unassigned” tabs.

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Step3
data.value: Click “Assign” on a role under “Unassigned Roles” to give it to the user; the change is saved at once.

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Step4
data.value: Click “Remove” on an assigned role, or the x beside it under “Active Roles”, and confirm to take it away.

data.name: Help.USERROLES.Immediate
data.value: Assigning and removing a role; a user gets the permissions of all their roles together

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Purpose
data.value: This page lists the items (materials kept in stock: active ingredients, excipients, packaging, intermediates) with their identity, material type and stock behaviour. Each item is created here and taken through its statuses: “Draft”, “Awaiting approval”, “Active”, “Deactivated”, “Retired”.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step1
data.value: Narrow the list with the search box, or click “Filter”, choose “Status” or “Material type” and click “Apply”.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step2
data.value: Click “Add item”, fill in the identity and the stock behaviour on its full-page form, then click “Save”: the item is saved as “Draft”. In a single-line field of that form, Enter saves it too (in the “Description” box Enter starts a new line). Later, on an active item only the name and the description change freely; a filled stock field needs an approved correction.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step3
data.value: Open a draft's “Actions” and choose “Send for approval”: the item stays “Awaiting approval” until it is approved, and only then becomes “Active”. While it is awaiting approval, the person who sent the request can choose “Withdraw Approval Request” in its “Actions”: the item goes back to its previous status.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step4
data.value: “Deactivate” takes an active item out of new stock entries; “Request reactivation” goes through the same approval again; “Retire” is final, is allowed only for a deactivated item with zero stock, and the code is never reused. Each of them asks for a reason.

data.name: Help.ITEMS.Step5
data.value: Outside a text field, with no dialog or side panel open, the “?” key opens this help with the page's shortcuts.
